name: Avalanche
executive_summary: Avalanche launched in September 2020 as a general-purpose smart-contract platform built around a fast, probabilistic consensus design rather than a single-purpose chain. That breadth shows up as real but not exceptional activity: several hundred thousand daily active addresses and multiple millions of daily transactions on the main smart-contract chain, alongside a broad institutional footprint -- six distinct named managers, including BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, and Janus Henderson, hold roughly $1 billion here. The TradFi score of 60 crosses into Emerging Institutional on the strength of that institutional access and two confirmed real-world-utility verticals, offset by a Decentralization score held down by a single validator software implementation despite a large, well-documented validator count. The AI score of 60 is anchored by a genuinely strong, currently-confirmed fee and throughput picture, offset by thin agent-specific tooling and no protocol-native way to verify an AI agent's identity.

key_findings: Avalanche clears our regulatory-access check outright: it's named directly in a March 2026 joint US regulatory interpretive release, and a spot ETF (VanEck's VAVX) has been trading on Nasdaq since January 2026, holding AVAX directly with staking rewards passed through to holders. No open government investigation or enforcement action was found against the team.

On-Chain Health (63) reflects genuine, sustained usage -- several hundred thousand daily active addresses and multiple millions of daily transactions, rising toward a recent peak near 3 million transactions in a single day. What's missing for a stronger score is the elite fee revenue seen on the very largest smart-contract platforms.

TradFi Approved (60) reflects a wide institutional footprint that has thinned since August 2026. BlackRock's tokenized fund held about 357 million tokens (roughly $357 million) on this chain on November 19, 2026, down from about $564 million in August, and Apollo's credit fund holds roughly $4.9 million. Two further global asset managers are live here: Franklin Templeton's BENJI fund ($34.2 million) and Janus Henderson's AAA CLO fund, deployed via Centrifuge at roughly $262 million. Galaxy Digital's CLO 2025-1 holds $17.9 million distributed on-chain. A tokenized natural-resource security, Bridgetower's DOM X Arizona copper-gold project, carries a real, transferable position of about $334 million here, separate from an unverified $11 billion headline valuation that earns no credit. VanEck's spot AVAX ETF held about $22 million at the end of September. Charles Schwab added AVAX to its tradable crypto list in November 2026. Six distinct institutional counterparties hold roughly $1 billion here today.

Real-World Utility (63) spans multiple genuinely separate verticals beyond the tokenized-fund and stablecoin activity above. Two independent verticals are confirmed live -- OpenTrade's real-world-yield platform ($200.7 million distributed on this chain) and Dinari's tokenized U.S. equities (over 350 tickers including SpaceX, though dollar value in this specific vertical stays modest). Different products serving different purposes, not the same story restated.

Tokenomics & Supply (60): AVAX has a 720 million hard cap with roughly 62% (about 447 million tokens) already circulating. The network still mints more in staking rewards than it burns in fees, so supply grows on net. The September 22, 2026 Helicon upgrade cut the minimum staking reward rate from 10% to 7.5%, phased in over 90 days to about December 21, 2026, which Ava Labs projects will lower annual inflation by 0.5 to 1 percentage point -- a live reduction in new issuance. A separate proposal to end net inflation entirely remains a proposal and earns no credit.

Decentralization (45) combines two separate checks. Counting independent validator entities looks strong at 24, enough to place Avalanche near the top of our mid-tier band on that measure alone -- but every validator runs the same consensus software with no independently built alternative to check it, which caps that reading lower. A second, separate check on where validators are physically and legally located lands lower still: roughly a quarter of measured nodes sit in a single country and a similar share sit with a single cloud provider. The lower of the two readings governs.

Privacy & Confidentiality (32): nearly everything on this chain is public by default. One encrypted-token standard has working code deployed, but shows zero recorded real-world usage, earning only minimal credit for existing.

Security & Future-Proofing (62): the one independent security audit on record found and fixed a serious bug before it could be exploited -- a flaw that could have let an attacker impersonate another user's identity in certain contract calls. But that audit predates three later network upgrades, including the September 2026 Helicon upgrade that changed how the main chain executes transactions, and no independent audit of the current code has been published. An active, funded bug bounty program is a positive; the team has no public post-quantum roadmap, though a co-founder said in October 2026 that an internal team is exploring post-quantum signature approaches.

Execution Layer (75) is a real strength: transactions cost a fraction of a cent, blocks arrive about once a second, and a live view of network activity has shown sustained throughput with headroom for roughly double the typical load. The September 2026 Helicon upgrade separated transaction execution from consensus so the chain can keep agreeing on new blocks while earlier ones finish executing; no measured throughput gain has been published yet, so it is not yet reflected in the score. Finality measures about 1.0 seconds at the median and 1.7 seconds at the 99th percentile -- fast for a probabilistic design, but short of guaranteed sub-second settlement.

Composability & Atomicity (78): all three of the standard tools an autonomous agent needs to batch multiple actions into one all-or-nothing transaction -- a multicall utility, a smart-account factory, and a token-approval standard -- are confirmed live and in active use on this chain today, not just theoretically available.

Security Posture (60) applies the same audit and client findings as the TradFi score, scored directly here rather than through a pass/fail gate. The bug caught and fixed before exploitation is a genuine positive signal; a documented history of application-level exploits elsewhere in the ecosystem is a real negative one.

State & API Quality (72): multiple independent, non-affiliated data providers exist for reading chain data, and a mature indexing service has supported developers for years. The real gap: a standard node keeps only about the last 32 blocks of history, so pulling older records requires a specialized archive node rather than the default setup.

Privacy & Confidentiality (24) mirrors the TradFi finding -- transparent by default. The one privacy-oriented tool live in code shows no real on-chain usage, and its intended deployment path points toward separate custom instances rather than this chain directly.

Economic Predictability (54): fees are protocol-enforced and low. Since the September 2026 Helicon upgrade, the minimum fee is set by a stake-weighted validator vote rather than fixed in the protocol; validators raised it from effectively zero to 5 nAVAX in late September, and the base fee sat near 7.5 nAVAX in mid-November -- roughly 100 times the pre-upgrade level, though still about a tenth of a cent per transfer. The floor can only double or halve over about an hour of sustained voting, but it has no upper limit. Working against predictability, a documented 2025 incident saw an attacker exploit the public pending-transaction pool to front-run trades (patched with rate-limiting rather than a structural fix), and no published policy commits to fair transaction ordering.

Agent Tooling (44) is thin. General smart-contract developer tools work fully here, but agent-specific infrastructure built directly on this chain is limited to one small community-built framework and one third-party agent wallet product, both with unconfirmed real adoption. A separate, purpose-built agent-identity blockchain has launched in the wider ecosystem, but it runs its own independent validators and is scored on its own terms, not credited here.

Standards & Interoperability (67): account abstraction -- letting a wallet run as programmable logic instead of a fixed key pair, so an agent can hold scoped permissions or spending limits -- isn't built into the protocol itself here, but the add-on infrastructure that provides it (bundlers and a paymaster integration) is live and already sees some real usage. The chain's own cross-chain messaging protocol connects it to the rest of its ecosystem without relying on third-party bridges -- a genuine strength for that specific reach. Connecting beyond that ecosystem still depends on bridges and oracle networks.

KYA (24): no protocol-native system exists for verifying or authorizing an AI agent's identity on this chain. One emerging cross-industry identity standard has a single demonstration deployment here, not real adoption, and a separate institutional compliance framework elsewhere in the ecosystem is aimed at human KYC, still pilot-stage, and not built for agents.

watch_items: Quantum-computer readiness has no official roadmap. The basis remains a community proposal from February 2026, though co-founder Emin Gün Sirer said in October 2026 that an internal team is exploring hash-based post-quantum signatures. Re-check whether this becomes a published plan.

A foundation proposal to move validator rewards toward a zero-inflation model, now supported by economics research grants, has no committed timeline -- a further Tokenomics & Supply re-credit candidate if it ships. The smaller Helicon reward-rate cut is already live and credited.
An encrypted-token privacy tool is live in code but shows no real usage yet -- a Privacy re-credit candidate on both scores if that changes.
Helicon's continuous execution has been live since September 22, 2026. A published, measured throughput gain under real load would be an Execution Layer re-credit candidate.
Account-abstraction infrastructure is live with real historical usage, but current volume is unconfirmed -- re-check adoption depth at the next reassessment.
The one security audit on record predates three subsequent network upgrades, including Helicon -- a new, current-scope audit would be a direct re-credit candidate on both scores.

A five-year, $240 billion contract to digitize 370,000 property deeds for a New Jersey county on this chain was signed in May 2025. As of this scoring, more than a year later, no public reporting shows it live -- no on-chain deed count, public search tool, or operational milestone was found anywhere. A genuine Real-World Utility and TradFi Approved re-credit candidate if it materializes; zero credit today per score-reality discipline.

Bridgetower's DOM X Arizona copper-gold project carries a real, transferable $333.6 million position on this chain, now reflected in TradFi Approved. The touted $11 billion total project valuation remains unverified as investor-held or transferable value and earns no credit -- re-check if a larger confirmed distributed position emerges.

A separate Japanese tokenization platform, Progmat, reported migrating over $2 billion in tokenized securities to this chain in 2026. Independently reported by multiple outlets, but the underlying securities are likely permissioned and non-transferable, and this figure isn't reflected in independent RWA trackers of this chain. Zero credit today; a re-credit candidate if a confirmed transferable position surfaces.

The New York Stock Exchange's planned 24/7 tokenized-securities platform, announced in January 2026 and targeting a fourth-quarter 2026 launch pending regulatory approval, was reported on November 9, 2026 to use this chain for clearing and settlement, after roughly a year of testing disclosed in September 2026. NYSE's own statement says this chain will provide the core ledger technology for the platform's clearing firm, while Ava Labs and press reports describe it as the exclusive settlement layer for a venue that also supports equities issued on multiple blockchains, so the exact scope is not yet pinned down. Nothing is live, so zero credit today per score-reality discipline; a TradFi Approved and Real-World Utility re-credit candidate once the platform launches and settles real trades here. It is not yet confirmed whether settlement would run on the public main chain or on a separate permissioned Avalanche chain; only the former would count toward this score.

The minimum transaction fee is now set by validator vote. Validators raised it from effectively zero to 5 nAVAX in late September 2026, and it sat near 7.5 nAVAX in mid-November. Further large moves, or evidence of how it behaves under load, would bear on the AI Economic Predictability score.
BlackRock's tokenized fund on this chain fell from about $564 million in August 2026 to about $357 million in November. Further outflows would weigh on TradFi Approved; a return would support it.

tiles.cheapest_tx_cost_note: Native transfer at the validator-set base fee of about 7.5 nAVAX (November 19, 2026).
